posts.name: cgrater
posts.cooked:
I appreciate that the gender/racial balances feel natural and not “forced”.

I also greatly appreciate the fact that >G has tastefully avoided the comic trend of rendering all female characters with improbable or downright impossible anatomies.

My gaming group is 50% female (awesome to have three great friends whose wives are all also gamers), and the female characters and their artistic treatment is part of what has made this game a continuous presence at our table. I backed for the enhanced edition, because we have literally worn out some of the decks in our original set. It has probably seen better than 200 games, all told. (We have even run two simultaneous games with one set…that was craziness).

Lessons that can be learned:
1.) Show women some respect, and they may actually enjoy your game.
2.) If you find a game that has followed lesson #1, sleeve the darn thing ASAP!

posts.name: beevolant
posts.cooked:
I think that the characters being a mix of races and genders (and besides Haka) their race/gender not really having anything to do with their powers is one of the things that make the SOTM world so interesting. Not that white men are not interesting, but… well, it’s been done (which is why Legacy is so tongue in cheek campy and awesome). I have already read/seen so many of their stories that when you read/see someone else’s story, it’s just so much fresher.

I think what I really like the most about the SOTM world is that it feels like how comics should be, as opposed to how they are. For two and a half white dudes from the midwest, that is pretty effing sweet.

I also really appreciate female characters who are not all boobs! OMG! I think Adam might be the only male artist drawing women who are not walking T&A shots (also, the women have pretty realistic super hero musculature, I totally dig that too). That’s not only really cool, but also really refreshing. Though, as a metal worker who has breasts and skin, I’ve got to say that I hope Unity wears a shirt more in the shop - unless she likes getting random burns/cuts/scratches or bits of metal polish in her belly button (and from personal experience, neither are fun!). I’m willing to let the safety issues of not having her tied back slide for the aesthetic but the exposed belly goes to far for my suspension of disbelief (see that whole personal experience with polishing grit in the belly button thing, don’t ask questions, I’m allowed to wear whatever I want in the privacy of my own basement and then learn my lesson). Besides the whole sports bra thing is kind of trite and reads 13-year-old-boy fantasy to me.
